title: Find the different Hugging Face tools
summary: Hugging Face includes a Hub for shared resources and libraries used in local programs. These are related tools with different jobs.
introduction: Hugging Face includes a Hub for shared resources and libraries used in local programs. These are related tools with different jobs. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain find the different hugging face tools
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Hugging Face includes a Hub for shared resources and libraries used in local programs. These are related tools with different jobs.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Python examples need the datasets and tokenizers packages in a separate environment. All sample data is written in the code. No Hub account, remote dataset or trained model download is needed.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Hugging Face. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
Hub: pages for models, datasets and other resources
Datasets library: load and transform data tables
Tokenizers library: turn text into token IDs
Transformers library: work with many model architectures
blocks.title: Find the different Hugging Face tools

blocks.text: The list separates the website from the libraries. The examples in this course use only local Datasets and Tokenizers features.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Name the tool you would use to transform a small data table.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A library installation does not mean a trained model has been downloaded.
For more detail later, use this [Hugging Face further reading](https://huggingface.co/docs).
